subject: Modeling covariates of interest in a multiple season analysis

messages.author: 827384b6e9f2b83b
messages.subject: Modeling covariates of interest in a multiple season analysis
parts:
Hi All,

I used a stratified random sampling design. 5 regions (strata) with 9 randomly selected sampling sites within each region, for a total of 45 sampling sites. Each site was sampled for a 7 night period 4 times each year (corresponding to bat reproductive cycles) during the 3 year study. This provided 84 discrete observations for each of the 45 sampling sites (7x4x3 = 84).


Each sampling site was categorized by habitat type - tree (1) or shrub (0). I am running a multiple season analysis and I’m interested in looking at the effect of habitat and region on occupancy, and the effect of habitat, reproductive cycle, and region on detection probability. None of the models of these covariates taken individually performed the best in single parameter models ((psi(.) gamma(.) epsilon(.)p(cycle)). However, combinations of covariates did ((psi(.) gamma(.) epsilon(.)p(cycle*region).

I have the following questions

  1. In order to look at the above mentioned effects on psi and p do I need to use the best model that incorporates all the covariates of interest (including those for gamma and epsilon) or do I run the best performing psi model separately from the best p model to see these effects?

    1. Would I run a GOF test first? If so is the parboot() function appropriate? Others on this forum (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!search/GOF$20colext/unmarked/LvLJj2xoe1s/uUch5vJKRlQJ) have suggested that there may be limitations to GOF tests for binary data such as mine but I could have misinterpreted that.

  2. Is a likelihood ratio test (LRT) appropriate for determining effects of these covariates on psi or p for colext models or is there another one? I’ve seen others on this forum using it to test the null hypothesis instead of the Wald z test that the summary gives you but only with occu.

  3. In addition to knowing how covariates affect psi and p I also want to present the best estimate of occupancy for each site and region. Would I use ranef() and the best, fully parameterized model to do this?

  4. Is Unmarked sufficient to look for differences in occupancy and detectability among regions and/or reproductive cycles? Bayesian Analysis has been suggested as a more robust method but as I am not a statistician I am unclear about this type of analysis. Am I correct in thinking that detecting effects of covariates on occupancy and detection probabilities is a different process from detecting actual differences in those parameters?


I think I may be confusing two different study goals with different approaches. I'm still researching when to use predict() and ranef() and how to best use them in this study. Any help is much appreciated. I really value the unmarked community’s input and have really benefitted from the contributors in the past. Thanks in advance.

Cheers,

Rachel
